text:
Maria C: Heads up — after the merge rolled to us-west2 (a10 pool) we're seeing a p99 regression on L4 models. Alerts fired at 10:12 UTC. Anyone on call?
Devon K: yep, saw the alert. perf-tests/latency -> a10-usw2 L4 p99 860ms -> ~2.1s on the smoke jobs. I'm pausing the rollout for the merge train. :hand: 
perf-ci-bot: [perf-tests/latency] job 2024-12-03T10:12 failed: p99 exceeded threshold (link: https://ci.internal/perf/12345)
Sachin R: I started a quick bisect locally. The suspect change is the kernel selector heuristic that landed in PR#5129 (merge-4062). When selector checks sequence-length hist it now prefers kernel B for 256+ tokens — overhead up more than expected on A10.
Olivia W: Profiling output from a repro run on a10 (short snippet):
```
hotspots:
- kernel_selector::choose_kernel 42% (was 18% pre-merge)
- batch_scheduler::wait_for_fill 28% -> increased locking contention
- kv_cache::spill_prefetch 15% (observed extra memcpy on NIC path)
```
Jamal T: interesting — on H100 runs the same workload is fine. suggests hardware-specific codepath in selector or nvlink vs nic path differences.
Devon K: infra graphs show NIC egress spikes on host-3 in the pool around the time of requests, could be noisy neighbor making kvspill worse. infra-bot can you isolate?
infra-bot: isolating host-3 from a10-usw2 pool and draining in-progress jobs. ETA 7m.
Maria C: good. Sachin, can you add a build with the selector change reverted and run the same smoke jobs? if that fixes canary we should roll back the change.
Sachin R: started build with revert (local tag: revert/kselector-5129). Kicking off perf smoke against a10 canary.
perf-ci-bot: perf run queued: https://ci.internal/perf/12346 (target: a10-usw2-canary)
Olivia W: additional note: batcher hysteresis parameter tweak (introduced in PR#5097) also interacts — I see longer wait_for_fill when selector prefers smaller-kernel packing which reduces throughput. Might be a two-change interaction.
Jamal T: suggestion: flip runtime flag `runtime.kselector.v2.enabled=false` in canary first, then revert PR if still broken. less risky.
Devon K: agreed. I'll stage a config toggle on the canary hosts and run perf.
Maria C: assign owners: Sachin for revert build + perf runs, Devon for canary toggle + infra isolation, Olivia to run flamegraph diff and post findings, Jamal to coordinate rollback plan if needed.
Sachin R: perf run complete on revert build — p99 back to ~870ms on canary. Revert seems to fix.
Devon K: after isolating host-3 and toggling the runtime flag on canary, p99 also dropped. Both mitigation paths work, so root cause likely selector + noisy NIC path causing kv spill memcopies to amplify.
Olivia W: uploading flamegraphs and annotated diff here: https://internal.artifacts/fg/1878012345/diff.html — choose_kernel and kv memcpy markers vanish on revert.
Maria C: OK, plan: 1) revert PR#5129 from merge-4062 in next hotfix release, 2) follow-up patch to make selector cost model aware of NIC memcpy cost on A10, 3) add a canary check in perf CI that runs selector-heavy workloads on A10.
Jamal T: +1. Also adding a guard to runtime flag to default-off v2 selector until we validate on all hardware.
Devon K: I'll keep rollout paused and will only resume once revert is in and perf CI green.
Sachin R: opening revert PR now: https://git.internal/r/revert-5129; adding description and tests.
Maria C: thanks all. filing a brief postmortem after we confirm the revert in prod. :memo:
perf-ci-bot: post-action: created issue PERF-8912 to track follow-ups (owners: Sachin, Olivia, Jamal).
Jamal T: note to self — add a small synthetic KV-prefetch test to our perf harness that hits the NIC path more to catch this.
Devon K: confirmed last check at 10:43 UTC — p99 on canary stable at 880ms. I'll update the incident channel once we fully revert.
Maria C: closing thread for now — follow-ups tracked in PERF-8912. Thanks everyone. :tada:
